item.title: Alternatives
item.description:
Java has no shortage of ways to talk to a database. This is a frank account of how YoSQL compares to the ones you are most likely choosing between, including where they are the better answer.

The short version

Where the query lives Runtime dependency Reflection Result mapping
YoSQL .sql files none none generated from a record
jOOQ Java DSL jOOQ some generated from the schema
MyBatis XML or annotations MyBatis yes configured
Spring Data JDBC derived names or @Query Spring yes convention
JDBI 3 annotations or fluent API JDBI yes mappers
Hibernate / JPA JPQL, criteria, derived names Hibernate yes mapped entities
Panache active record or repository Quarkus + Hibernate build-time indexed mapped entities

Where YoSQL wins

Nothing ships with your application. YoSQL runs during the build and leaves Java behind. There is no library on the runtime classpath, no version to keep in step with your framework, and no upgrade that changes how your queries behave. You can stop using YoSQL at any point by keeping the generated code — see the command line tool .
